part-1.2.1.scope: Chemical elements — 118 recognized kinds, corresponding to atomic numbers 1–118; applies to Atom and Elemental substance portion. Element 119 is not an accepted discovery.
part-1.2.1.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-1.1.2.scope: Elementary particles — 17 Standard Model kinds in the conventional chart: six quark flavours, six leptons, four gauge-boson kinds, and the Higgs boson. Antiparticles and colour states are not counted separately; this is not a count of all composite subatomic particles.
part-1.1.2.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-2.1.4.scope: Minerals — 6,239 valid mineral species, IMA-CNMNC master list, 2026.09; kinds represented by Mineral substance portion, not individual mineral grains.
part-2.1.4.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-1.3.2.scope: Stars — more than 100 billion in the Milky Way, an estimated population within our galaxy.
part-1.3.2.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-1.3.2.scope: Galaxies — at least 100 billion in the observable universe, NASA's broad estimate; faint-galaxy extrapolations depend on detection limits and cosmological models.
part-1.3.2.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-2.2.2.scope: Oceans — five named oceans within one connected global ocean; applies to Saltwater area.
part-2.2.2.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-2.2.2.scope: Lakes — about 117 million with area at least 0.002 km², the GLOWABO satellite inventory (2014), excluding Greenland and Antarctica. A size-threshold estimate relevant to Standing-water area; lakes are not necessarily freshwater.
part-2.2.2.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-5.2.4.scope: Humans — about 8.3 billion living individuals in 2026, a rounded global population estimate, not a count of everyone who has ever lived.
part-5.2.4.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-4.2.1.scope: Bones — 206 in the conventional adult human skeleton; individual variation and counting of fused bones can change the count. Applies to anatomical bones, not kinds of Bone tissue portion.
part-4.2.1.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-4.2.1.scope: Muscles — more than 600 in a human body; anatomical count varies with grouping, not a count of muscle-tissue kinds.
part-4.2.1.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-4.2.1.scope: Chromosomes — 46, arranged in 23 pairs, in a typical human diploid cell; gametes and chromosomal variants have different counts.
part-4.2.1.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-3.3.1.scope: Cells — about 36 trillion in a reference adult male and 28 trillion in a reference adult female, Hatton et al. (2023); model-dependent individual counts, not cell-type counts or a total for all organisms.
part-3.3.1.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.

part-5.1.4.scope: Human languages — 7,170 living languages, Ethnologue's 29th edition (2026), as reported by Wikipedia. Language-versus-dialect boundaries depend on the catalogue; extinct and constructed languages are outside this total.
part-5.1.4.interpretation: A scoped reference count for the named subject within this outline topic, not a total for every topic member.
